text:
Juraj Slafkovský has two goals in 26 games. The first overall pick in 2022, coming off an Olympics where he had eight points in six games for Slovakia, is shooting 3.5% this season, and he has heard about it; he told reporters he knows he needs to be better.

Half of this is bad luck. He has 8.7 expected goals, the quality of his chances, and turned them into two. Goals tend to follow chances, and few forwards in the league are owed more. He's still playing over 18 minutes a night and getting six of his 14 points on the power play.

The other half is harder to wave off. Over his last ten games he has two points and no goals, and the chances have dried up too: Montreal is on the ice for clearly fewer expected goals with him out there than usual. Evolving-Hockey flagged last season that opponents created a lot against him while he faced top competition, and his five-on-five chance share is under 48% again. With Dylan Larkin now in Montreal, his role could shift. Watch the chances first. The goals should come if those come back.
headline: Slafkovský is owed goals, but not all of them
